description: FasalShift — an Urdu-first wheat rotation planner for Punjab, Pakistan, using NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, SMAP and Landsat data. We are a two-person team from the University of Agriculture Faisalabad: Umar Shareef (BSCS final year) and Naveed Ahmad.
summary: FasalShift tells a Punjab wheat farmer which rotation to plant next — from 22 years of live NASA data — and how many days late they can still plant. It measures the monsoon-onset shift from 22 years of NASA POWER daily data (Faisalabad: +2 days since 2004), scores three rotations (Wheat→Pulses wins at 7.2/10), and stress-tests each one to find the last safe planting day (Faisalabad: 2 days of slip). Urdu-first, with a spoken Urdu summary. Every number is live from NASA POWER or a labelled rule — nothing invented, no pilot users yet (stated in the app).
details: Next.js 14 + TypeScript app. A deterministic rotation engine (no LLM): monsoon onset detection (3-day ≥ 7.5 mm rule), OLS trend test, growing-degree-day and grain-fill heat-day math, 4-dimension rotation scoring (water 35%, soil 25%, heat 25%, margin 15%), and an Adaptation Margin stress test that slides the planting window over the real 2024-25 daily series. Urdu-first UI with English toggle and a Web Speech API Urdu voice summary. Live data proxied through /api/nasa/power (15-min cache, −999 fill values stripped, never averaged). Sources page cites every dataset. Use of AI: The product engine is deterministic — no LLM in the product, no ML model: monsoon-onset rule, OLS trend test, GDD/heat math, labelled-rule rotation scoring, and the Adaptation Margin stress test are all hand-written, transparent code (see docs/ROTATION-SCORING.md). AI-assisted coding was used during the sprint to write and review that code and these docs; every number the app shows comes from live NASA data or a labelled rule, and every claim was verified against the live APIs before submission. Results (verified, Sat Nov 14, 2026): - 42/42 unit tests passing (rotation engine + shift math + CMR response shaping); tsc clean; next build clean. - Faisalabad: onset +2 days (2004 Jun 16 → recent median Jun 18); trend −0.54 days/yr, p = 0.12 — NOT statistically significant (reported honestly). - GDD 2,416 → 2,681; grain-fill heat days 0 → 5. - Rotations (Faisalabad): Pulses 7.2 ★, Cotton 6.2, Maize 6.0 (water scoring input capped at 1.0× — labelled rule; the 2025 wet year is 2.12× climatology, displayed true, scored as 1.0×). - Adaptation Margin: Faisalabad 2 days (all rotations); Multan 8; Layyah 3; Lahore 2. - Multi-district onsets regenerated to the full 2004–2025 series from live NASA POWER (n = 22 for all four districts; previously n = 4 for Lahore/Multan/Layyah — a cache-generation gap, not real data). Median shifts unchanged: Lahore +12, Multan −5, Layyah −4. Trends (n = 22): Multan −1.76 days/yr, p = 0.004 — statistically significant (onset earlier); Lahore −0.17 days/yr, p = 0.62; Layyah −0.58 days/yr, p = 0.07 — not significant. - 2025 monsoon: 5.02 mm/day vs 2.37 climatology = 2.12× (wet year). - Satellite context live in-app (/api/nasa/cmr): latest Faisalabad HLS granule Oct 29, 2026; ECOSTRESS Oct 31, 2026 — metadata only, no processing pipeline. Next step: pilot via Punjab agriculture extension SMS networks, to be piloted — no contact yet. Limits (stated in the app + deck, do not hide): - Onset trend not significant (p = 0.12); headline is the +2-day median shift. - Soil moisture is ERA5 reanalysis, not SMAP; rain is POWER (~50 km), not IMERG. - No Landsat/ECOSTRESS processing pipeline (metadata only); no ML rotation model. - No pilot users yet; no farmer field validation. - POWER data lags ~2 days; newest days show as "not yet published". Open-source repo: https://github.com/umarshareef0165-netizen/fasalshift
